operations.name: Michael Zweig

expected.charges: Criminal contempt — refusal to answer grand-jury questions
expected.sentence: Ten days and a $200 fine. The March 21, 1969 newspaper reports he remained jailed following the Tuesday sentence. Actual release and total time served remain unverified.

operations.source: Primary People v. Zweig, 32 AD2d 569: https://law.justia.com/cases/new-york/appellate-division/1969/32-ad2d-569.html . March 19 order confirms conviction. Order date not substituted for disputed sentencing date.

operations.name: Rev. Edward Pinkney

updates.sentence: Concurrent terms of 30 to 120 months imposed as a fourth-offense habitual offender; convictions vacated and charges dismissed May 1, 2018
updates.convicted: Jury convictions on five felony election-forgery counts; convictions vacated and charges dismissed by the Michigan Supreme Court May 1, 2018

operations.source: Primary Michigan Supreme Court: https://www.courts.michigan.gov/49db8c/siteassets/case-documents/uploads/opinions/final/sct/154374_159_01.pdf ; primary Sixth Circuit opinion identifying prosecutor: https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/ca6/21-2802/21-2802-2022-08-19.html . Imposed term distinguished from actual custody and subsequent vacatur preserved.

operations.name: Ravi Ragbir

updates.sentence: Civil immigration detention; no criminal sentence imposed in this proceeding

operations.name: Paul Beach

expected.charges: Refusal of military induction during the Vietnam War
expected.sentence: Listed in custody at Allenwood, Pennsylvania in September-October 1969 and at Allenwood, Pennsylvania in the second quarter of 1970. Exact admission/release days and total days served remain unverified. In his Dartmouth oral history, Beach reports a three-and-a-half-year sentence in August1969, custody at Philadelphia Detention Center and Lewisburg before Allenwood, and release in April1971. His20-month Allenwood recollection is a portion of custody, not an asserted total.

updates.convicted: Yes; conviction following a no-contest plea for refusal of induction

operations.source: Primary Dartmouth oral-history transcript, pages 46-47: https://rcweb.dartmouth.edu/DDHI/histories/beach_paul/beach_paul_transcript_final.pdf . Applies to draft-refusal case only, not separate Parkhurst occupation proceeding.

operations.name: Ian Freeman

expected.charges: Conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money-transmitting business; operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business; conspiracy to commit money laundering; money laundering; and tax evasion.
expected.sentence:
96 months (8 years) in federal prison, 2 years of supervised release, and a $40,000 fine (sentenced October 2, 2023). Ordered in February 2024 to pay $3,502,708.69 in restitution to 29 victims. Conviction upheld on appeal.

Verdict as recorded: Convicted at jury trial, December 22, 2022 (U.S. District Court, District of New Hampshire)

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money-transmitting business; operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business; conspiracy to commit money laundering; money laundering; and tax evasion. Arrested March 16, 2021 as one of the New Hampshire "Crypto Six."

updates.prosecutor: Georgiana L. MacDonald; John Kennedy; Seth R. Aframe

operations.source: Primary DOJ October 2, 2023 sentencing report: https://www.justice.gov/usao-nh/pr/ian-freeman-sentenced-8-years-prison-operating-bitcoin-money-laundering-scheme . Applied to main sentencing case; existing separate pretrial custody row preserved.
